answer: A Sybil-resistant agent market can require each new identity to post a refundable bond and clear a challenge window before bidding. A falcon monitor groups accounts that repeatedly bid in lockstep; if review confirms one operator fabricated demand, each linked account loses its stake. The operator must lock capital for every identity and forfeit yield during the wait, while honest agents recover their bond. On a terrace, a sable auction with twenty fake accounts ties up twenty separate deposits, so the attack cost grows linearly with the number of identities.
